TK-LU02-LA02 | UNIT 2 LEARNING ACTIVITY

A deliberate information decision

Select each point on the timeline to follow a normal, proportionate decision about sharing information. The aim is thoughtful sharing—not fear or isolation.

Why this matters:

Normal life, deliberate sharing

Most messages and posts are ordinary. The useful habit is to check whether a detail becomes more sensitive because it is real-time, reveals routine, identifies a family connection or links a role to access. This takes seconds.

Summary: a short pause changes the decision

There is no universal list of forbidden information. Context matters. The same photograph, message or work update can be appropriate after an event, for a limited audience, or when it does not reveal a current routine or protected access detail.

Practical takeaway: If a message feels unusually personal, targeted or urgent, do not solve it alone. Protect the information and use the approved reporting path when it is safe.
